function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning: The user wants to start Docker on Windows using docker start. They want to execute a command. We can use the cmd_controller_execute function. The command would be something like "docker start <container_name>" but they didn't specify container name. Maybe they want to start Docker service? Actually "docker start" starts a container. To start Docker service, you might use "net start com.docker.service". But the user says "start Docker on window using docker start." That seems ambiguous. They might want to start Docker Desktop service. But "docker start" is used to start containers. So maybe they want to start Docker Desktop. But the correct command to start Docker Desktop service is "net start com.docker.service". Or "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service" in PowerShell. But the user explicitly says "using docker start". That might be a mistake. But we can interpret as they want to start Docker Desktop service. So we can run "net start com.docker.service". Let's do that.
